cli_cases.sql: CREATE EVENT golden_ev ON SCHEDULE EVERY 1 DAY DISABLE DO DELETE FROM t

statement_sql: CREATE EVENT golden_ev ON SCHEDULE EVERY 1 DAY DISABLE DO DELETE FROM t

cli_cases.notes: Golden path: a DISABLED event still audits its DO body — the where blocker lands on member 0 with event scope metadata while the lifecycle notice stays at the head; disabled means unaudited-execution, never unaudited-body.

cli_cases.sql: CREATE EVENT ev ON SCHEDULE EVERY 1 DAY DISABLE DO DELETE FROM t WHERE id = 1
cli_cases.notes: A WHERE-guarded body produces no blocker and the disabled event produces no execution warning.

cli_cases.sql: CREATE EVENT ev ON SCHEDULE EVERY 1 HOUR ENABLE DO SELECT 1
cli_cases.notes: An ENABLED repeating event surfaces the scheduled-execution warning with schedule shape metadata; the audit never predicts a runtime outcome.

cli_cases.sql: CREATE EVENT ev ON SCHEDULE AT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP DO SELECT 1
cli_cases.notes: A one-shot AT schedule still schedules execution — the warning distinguishes repeating=False.

cli_cases.sql: ALTER EVENT ev DISABLE ON SLAVE
cli_cases.notes: DISABLE ON SLAVE stops replicas only — the event still executes on the primary, so the warning fires with the authored status.

cli_cases.sql: ALTER EVENT ev ON SCHEDULE EVERY 2 DAY
cli_cases.notes: An ALTER that authors no status clause leaves the enabled-execution premise unproven — an explicit catalog gap, never a guessed warning.

cli_cases.sql: ALTER EVENT ev DO DELETE FROM t
cli_cases.notes: A DO-only ALTER replaces the body — it audits through the member machinery (blocker on member 0) while the missing status clause still owes the enabled-state gap.
A full DISABLE stops the schedule — no warning and no enabled-state gap.
DROP EVENT emits its lifecycle notice.

cli_cases.sql: CREATE EVENT ev ON SCHEDULE EVERY 1 DAY DISABLE DO BEGIN DELETE FROM audit_log; UPDATE t SET x = 1 WHERE id = 1; END
cli_cases.notes: A BEGIN…END DO body audits its members through the shared machinery — the unguarded DELETE blocks on member 0.

cli_cases.sql: CREATE DEFINER='root'@'localhost' EVENT ev ON SCHEDULE EVERY 1 DAY DISABLE DO SELECT 1
cli_cases.notes: The DEFINER clause is modeled as a shape; the account payload never reaches the declaration.

cli_cases.sql: CREATE EVENT ev ON SCHEDULE EVERY 1 DAY STARTS '2027-01-01 00:00:00' ENDS '2027-06-01 00:00:00' ON COMPLETION PRESERVE DISABLE DO SELECT 1
cli_cases.notes: STARTS/ENDS bounds and ON COMPLETION PRESERVE are modeled schedule attributes; clock values are captured, never evaluated.

cli_cases.sql: CREATE EVENT ev ON SCHEDULE EVERY 1 DAY DISABLE DO BEGIN DELETE FROM audit_log; UPDATE t SET x=1 WHERE id=1; END; SELECT 1

statement_sql: CREATE EVENT ev ON SCHEDULE EVERY 1 DAY DISABLE DO BEGIN DELETE FROM audit_log; UPDATE t SET x=1 WHERE id=1; END;

cli_cases.notes: The compound DO body keeps member semicolons inside the statement; the following SELECT lands as statement 2.

cli_cases.sql: CREATE EVENT ev ON SCHEDULE EVERY
cli_cases.notes: A truncated schedule declines the recognizer and stays a parser error — never fabricated audit.
